# cryoglyph (vendored)

- **Upstream:** https://github.com/iced-rs/cryoglyph.git
- **Revision:** `cf38ed5ea0cfe95270b31ced2910560a7fcc5003`
- **Copied:** 2026-11-06, from the checkout cargo had fetched for this revision (decision N2, `docs/native/decisions/0002-vendored-iced.md`).
- **Left out:** `benches/`, `examples/`, `samples/`, `.github/`.
- **Manifest edits:** `[dev-dependencies]` and the `[[bench]]` target. Its `cosmic-text` git dependency is patched to the copy beside it by `engine/Cargo.toml`.

Licences are kept as shipped. Every source file the crates compile, and every file they `include_bytes!`/`include_str!`, is present.

## Local fixes

None yet. Each fix to this copy gets an entry here: what changed, why, and the upstream issue or pull request link, so
that the copy can be replaced by a newer upstream revision without losing or forgetting a fix.

- **S2t, Chromium's baseline** (`src/text_render.rs`, `baseline`): glyph rows are placed on `round((line_top + round(ascent) + floor((line_height - round(ascent) - round(descent)) / 2)) * scale)` instead of `round(line_y * scale)`, using the new `LayoutRun::line_ascent` and `line_descent`. Why: Chromium rounds the font metrics in logical pixels and floors the half leading, so the same text sat up to one pixel off in rows and 70 of 98 rows were a pixel off at 150 % when the metrics were rounded at the drawn size (`docs/native/typography.md`, section 4).

- **S2c, subpixel text and Skia's coverage adjustment** (`shader.wgsl`, `cache.rs`, `text_atlas.rs`, `text_render.rs`, `viewport.rs`, `lib.rs`): a text area may ask for subpixel coverage (`TextArea::subpixel`). Such a glyph is rasterized with `CacheKeyFlags::LCD` and stored in the mask atlas three texels per pixel (`ContentType::Lcd`, `atlas_texels`); the fragment shader reads the three texels of its pixel and blends each channel by its own coverage with a second fragment output (`dual_source_blending`, blend factors `Src1`/`OneMinusSrc1`, which for grayscale and colour glyphs is ordinary alpha blending). The shader is built in two variants (`//@dual:` and `//@single:` blocks, `cache::shader_source`): on a device without `DUAL_SOURCE_BLENDING` there is no subpixel entry and text stays grayscale (`TextAtlas::subpixel_supported`). `Viewport::set_rendering` sets the order of the subpixels and Skia's coverage adjustment (`SkMaskGamma`: contrast and gamma applied per channel, or to the colour's luminance for grayscale, with the text colour quantized to three bits as Skia does); the uniform buffer is visible to the fragment stage. Why: today's app draws ClearType text and Chromium's luminance-dependent coverage (`docs/native/typography.md`, section 6). Device-level tests are in `engine/crates/styk-text-check/tests/text_pipeline.rs` (a vendored crate cannot carry dev-dependencies).
- **S2d, glyph masks from a worker** (`raster.rs`, `text_render.rs`, `text_atlas.rs`, `viewport.rs`, `lib.rs`, `shader.wgsl`): when `Viewport::set_rendering` says `direct_write`, `prepare` does not rasterize a glyph on the calling thread: it takes the mask a worker thread ("glyphs") has drawn with `cosmic_text::dwrite`, or asks the worker for it, leaves that glyph out of this frame and reports `TextRenderer::incomplete()`; a glyph the worker cannot draw (colour fonts, no DirectWrite) is rasterized by swash as before. `glyphs_pending()` counts the glyphs asked and not yet used, and `set_glyph_notifier` is called when the worker has drawn some, so the program asks for another frame. The atlas now grows by copying the old texture into the new one (it re-rasterized every glyph before, which would have meant drawing them all again). The subpixel masks are R, G, B order, so the shader swaps channels only for a BGR display. Non-Windows builds have a stub worker that only reports unsupported.
- **S2e, the worker protocol and candidate frames** (`raster.rs` rewritten, `text_render.rs`, `viewport.rs`, `lib.rs`): the worker ("glyphs") draws with DirectWrite or swash (`GlyphDrawing`); colour fonts, DirectWrite failures and the glyphs with `FAKE_ITALIC`, `DISABLE_HINTING` or `PIXEL_FONT` are swash's, on the worker. The interface thread owns its bookkeeping (`Client`, thread-local) and shares no lock with the worker: requests go through a bounded queue with nonblocking admission (`MAX_JOBS`, `MAX_INFLIGHT_BYTES` per interface thread), results come back on the thread's own channel (`MAX_READY_BYTES`). A frame is a candidate (`begin_candidate`, `end_candidate`): a request it does not touch again is obsolete when it ends, the worker skips its job (a shared floor) and its result is dropped on arrival, so nothing superseded stays pending (the old global pending count never fell for an abandoned request). `prewarm` queues glyphs ahead of any frame (results wait, `MAX_WARM_BYTES`). The viewport carries `GlyphDrawing` and `aliased` (`TextRendering`); `TextRenderer::prepare` sets `ALIASED` instead of `LCD` for unsmoothed text. The old `glyphs_pending` and the sync swash fallback in `prepare` are gone.
- **S2f, consumers, byte reservations and worker failures** (`raster.rs`, `viewport.rs`, `lib.rs`, `text_render.rs`): the glyph client is per `Viewport` (one per renderer) instead of thread-local, so one window's candidates never retire another's requests and replies find who asked (`Viewport::{begin_candidate, end_candidate, glyph_state}`). Every job holds a `Reservation` against a shared byte budget (`FRAME_BYTES`; the warm glyphs have `WARM_BYTES`), made before the job is queued and held through the worker, the reply queue and the consumer's store until the mask is uploaded; DirectWrite checks the exact size before it allocates; a mask that does not fit answers `Overflow` and the request comes back with the size learned; one mask larger than the budget passes alone. The warm glyphs wait on a shared shelf (`try_lock` only) that every window reads. A `Ticket` answers "lost" when a job is dropped unanswered (the worker died), a DirectWrite panic is drawn again by swash, and a dead worker is replaced by the next request. Test seams (`slow_worker`, `fail_draws`, `kill_worker`, `overflow_draws`, `set_frame_budget`, `skipped_jobs`) are `doc(hidden)`.
